01 · My story

A journey built step by step.

Not just a list of courses — this is how my interests, experiences and projects shaped the direction I am taking today.

Where it started2022 · B.E. Computer Engineering

Building the foundation

My college journey at SG Balekundri Institute of Technology (SGBIT), Belagavi gave me a strong foundation in programming, databases, software development and problem solving. Early on, I noticed that the part of engineering I enjoyed most wasn't just writing code — it was making sense of data and using it to answer real questions.

Learning beyond the classroomCollege journey

Exploring data analytics, hands-on

Outside my regular coursework, I actively picked up SQL, Excel, Power BI and Python through certifications and self-driven projects — learning to clean messy data, write meaningful queries, build data models, and design dashboards that actually communicate something. Every project pushed me from "I know this tool" to "I know when and why to use it," which is what eventually became the analytics work in my Projects section.

Community & leadership experienceSHE Innovates Program

SHE Innovates — where I grew beyond technical skills

One of the most defining parts of my college life was being selected for the SHE Innovates program, a college-level initiative built around women in innovation, entrepreneurship and leadership. Being part of it pushed me well outside my comfort zone — from handling student and event data, to coordinating logistics, to representing my team and communicating ideas clearly in front of mentors and peers.

It wasn't a technical internship, but it shaped how I approach technical work today — with more structure, more ownership, and more confidence to speak up. It also gave me a close look at how ideas move from a concept to something real, which is exactly the mindset I now bring into every data project I take on.

What I took from it: leadership under real deadlines, comfort working with ambiguous, unstructured information, stronger communication and presentation skills, and a genuine appreciation for how data, people and entrepreneurship intersect.
AI / ML experienceVTU VRIF · 2026

Stepping into AI and machine learning

During my AI/ML Prompt Engineer internship at VTU VRIF, I went deeper into Python, NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and core machine-learning concepts, and built an AI Skin Analyze project using TensorFlow and Keras — covering image preprocessing, model training and prediction. This was my first real experience of the full ML lifecycle: from raw, messy data all the way to a working, testable model.

Current chapter2026 · PySpiders Internship

Interning at PySpiders — Data Analytics, Data Science & GenAI

I am currently interning at PySpiders, where I am deepening my skills in Data Analytics, Data Science and Generative AI in a structured, project-driven environment. This includes sharpening my Python and SQL fundamentals, working through statistics and machine-learning workflows (from data cleaning and EDA to model building and evaluation), and learning how Generative AI tools and prompting techniques can be used practically inside real analytics and automation workflows.

This internship is where everything I've learned so far — analytics thinking from my projects, technical depth from VTU VRIF, and the confidence and ownership from SHE Innovates — is coming together into one connected skill set.

Currently strengthening: Python for data science, SQL, statistics for ML, model building & evaluation, and applied Generative AI / prompting workflows.

03 · Data Analytics Projects

Projects that made the learning real.

Hands-on work across SQL, Power BI, Excel and Python — with each project focused on turning raw data into useful business insights.

01PYTHON · SQL · POWER BI

Customer Behavior Dashboard

Segmentation, discount, and revenue analysis for an e-commerce customer base.

PROBLEM IDENTIFIED

The business had raw transaction-level customer data but no clear view of who its highest-value customers were, which segments to target, or what was actually driving revenue.

WHAT I BUILT

Pulled and cleaned data with Python (pandas, SQLAlchemy) from MySQL, wrote SQL to segment customers into new / returning / loyal groups, and built a Power BI dashboard to visualize the results.

KEY FINDINGS
  • 3.9K customers analyzed — $59.8 average purchase amount, 3.75/5 average review rating.
  • Only 27% of customers were active subscribers vs 73% non-subscribers.
  • Clothing was the top revenue and sales category, ahead of Accessories, Footwear, and Outerwear.
  • Middle-aged customers generated the highest revenue and sales volume of any age group.
  • Ranked the top 3 best-selling items per category using SQL window functions (ROW_NUMBER).
PythonpandasSQLAlchemyMySQLPower BI
View project on GitHub ↗
02POWER BI · DAX · DATA MODELING

Retail Store Dashboard

Multi-page Power BI report on sales, profit, and channel performance.

Overview page
Time series page
PROBLEM IDENTIFIED

Retail sales data was spread across regions, cities, brands, and channels with no single view connecting revenue to profitability — so it wasn't clear which regions were actually the most valuable, not just the biggest.

WHAT I BUILT

Built a multi-page Power BI report covering total sales and profit, regional and channel breakdowns, and category-level profit tracking across Beauty, Grocery, Home, Electronics, and Clothing.

KEY FINDINGS
  • Tracked 49.64M in total sales and 11.23M in profit across 500 customers, 5K orders, and 200 products.
  • South region led in sales volume, but East delivered the highest profit share (42% of total profit).
  • Online vs in-store channels were nearly evenly split (49.4% vs 50.6% of sales).
  • Built brand and city-level breakdowns to pinpoint where revenue was concentrated.
Power BIDAXData Modeling

03EXCEL · PIVOT TABLES · SLICERS

Zepto Sales Analysis

Pivot-table dashboard tracking revenue and order fulfillment for a quick-commerce grocery business.

Full view
Filtered: Mumbai · Frozen
PROBLEM IDENTIFIED

Order-level data for a quick-commerce grocery business needed to be turned into a usable view of revenue, refunds, and delivery performance across cities and product categories.

WHAT I BUILT

Built a fully interactive Excel dashboard using pivot tables and slicers, letting the business filter product-level sales trends by city and category.

KEY FINDINGS
  • Tracked 1,500 customers with 564.0K in revenue and 72.8K in refunds.
  • 84% of orders were successfully delivered; cancellations (8%), failed orders (5%), and returns (3%) tracked separately.
  • Built city-wise (Bangalore, Delhi, Mumbai) and category-wise breakdowns across Bakery, Beverages, Dairy, Frozen, Fruits, and more.
